name: Explorer 1

parts.name: Whip antennas
parts.role: Send data down to ground tracking stations
parts.snap: Whip antennas attached. Ready to beam data home.

parts.name: Nose cone
parts.role: Aerodynamic point that shielded the instruments during launch

parts.name: Geiger counter section
parts.snap: Geiger counter installed. This part made the breakthrough.

parts.name: Battery section
parts.role: Mercury batteries that powered the transmitters
parts.snap: Batteries secured. They will run for 31 days.

parts.name: Electronics section
parts.role: High and low power radio telemetry transmitters

parts.name: Tail section
parts.snap: Tail attached. Explorer 1 stayed attached to its final stage.

challenge.title: Find the radiation belts
challenge.intro: Slide the satellite along its orbit and watch the Geiger counter. Log three readings: low, middle, and high.
challenge.hint: Explorer 1's counter did something strange up high. Slide all the way up and see.

signal_note: Explorer 1 fell silent after 105 days, but orbited silently for over a decade before atmospheric re-entry.
ending: Explorer 1 discovered Earth's radiation belts, opening the era of scientific space discovery.
